claims.quote: A neutrophil is a phagocytic cell that is attracted via chemotaxis from the bloodstream to infected tissues. These spherical cells are granulocytes.

source.section: 21.2 Barrier Defenses and the Innate Immune Response
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: The most common of all the leukocytes, neutrophils will normally comprise 50–70 percent of total leukocyte count. They are 10–12 µm in diameter, significantly larger than erythrocytes.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: Neutrophils have a nucleus with two to five lobes, and they contain organelles, called lysosomes, that digest engulfed pathogens.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: The nucleus has a distinct lobed appearance and may have two to five lobes, the number increasing with the age of the cell.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: slender chromatin threads connecting the nuclear lobes
claims.quote: a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin

claims.value: neutrophilic granules (show up most clearly with chemically neutral stains); look: quite fine, normally light lilac; abundance: many; position: unknown
claims.quote: They are called neutrophils because their granules show up most clearly with stains that are chemically neutral (neither acidic nor basic). The granules are numerous but quite fine and normally appear light lilac.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A rapid responder and efficient phagocyte that prefers bacteria, it carries lysozyme in its granules to break down bacterial cell walls.
claims.quote: Neutrophils are rapid responders to the site of infection and are efficient phagocytes with a preference for bacteria. Their granules include lysozyme, an enzyme capable of lysing, or breaking down, bacterial cell walls

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its granules also carry oxidants such as hydrogen peroxide and defensins, proteins that pierce the membranes of bacteria and fungi so their contents leak out.
claims.quote: Their granules include lysozyme, an enzyme capable of lysing, or breaking down, bacterial cell walls; oxidants such as hydrogen peroxide; and defensins, proteins that bind to and puncture bacterial and fungal plasma membranes, so that the cell contents leak out.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its lysosomes digest the pathogens it engulfs.
claims.quote: A neutrophil is also a phagocytic leukocyte that engulfs and digests pathogens. Neutrophils, shown in , are the most abundant leukocytes of the immune system. Neutrophils have a nucleus with two to five lobes, and they contain organelles, called lysosomes, that digest engulfed pathogens.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A spherical granulocyte and phagocyte, it is drawn by chemotaxis out of the bloodstream into infected tissue.
claims.quote: A neutrophil is a phagocytic cell that is attracted via chemotaxis from the bloodstream to infected tissues. These spherical cells are granulocytes.

source.section: 21.2 Barrier Defenses and the Innate Immune Response
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.
tier1.attribution: Definition from the Cell Ontology (CL 2026-06-08), CL:0000775. CC BY 4.0.
